data.hypothesis: Prior results include five distinct valid programs: dynamic rows with chunk 1 measured 0.28208 s, cyclic static rows 0.28344 s, collapsed 2D dynamic chunks of 256 0.28388 s, guided rows 0.30548 s, and contiguous static rows 0.36279 s. These separate runs do not establish why their timings differ. This candidate tests whether dynamic row chunks of 4 reduce dispatch overhead relative to chunk 1 while retaining some load balancing; larger row batches may instead increase imbalance. The scalar recurrence, float coordinates, serial path for a one-thread team, and thread cap remain unchanged.

memory_lessons.applicability: Use these measurements to motivate a chunk-size comparison, not to infer scheduling cause or per-core performance; measure the new variant at the requested core counts and sizes.
memory_lessons.claim: The five recorded distinct valid programs had means spanning 0.28208–0.36279 s: dynamic rows with chunk 1 was fastest in those runs, while contiguous static rows was slowest. The source-diversity catalog reports five distinct programs and no repeats; these measurements do not establish results for a different dynamic chunk size.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure dynamic row scheduling with chunk 4 against the existing variants at one and four threads, including n=1024, smaller sizes, and shifted bounds.

data.notes: This is a scheduling-granularity experiment only. The supplied prior means are from separate runs and are not a measurement or confirmation of this candidate; leave correctness and performance evaluation to the controller.
transformations: Changed the parallel row loop from contiguous static scheduling to OpenMP dynamic scheduling with chunk size 4.
Retained the serial path, team-size cap, original float coordinate expressions, scalar recurrence, and per-pixel output writes.
